newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia's Nusamba buying large Astra stake - paper.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's Nusamba buying large Astra stake - paper.

text.p: A group linked to President Suharto will buy a large stake in Indonesia's biggest automobile manufacturer Astra International and could form a consortium with other major shareholders, a newspaper said on Saturday.
Kompas newspaper quoted Nusamba Group head Muhamad "Bob" Hasan as saying that he had reached an agreement to buy all the shares in Astra owned by state-owned banks and pension funds.
"We have an agreement with government banks and their pension funds to buy shares that they want to sell," he was quoted as saying.
Nusamba would buy a stake of about 10 percent in Astra at a slight premium to prevailing market prices some time next week, said Hassan who gave no further details.

Kompas quoted Hasan as also saying that Nusamba will hold talks with other large shareholders in the company to form a consortium. "By working together, we can improve shareholder value," he was quoted as saying.
Hasan was not available for comment.
Nusamba is 80 percent owned by three foundations headed by Suharto. Hasan, a close associate of Suharto, and the president's eldest son Sigit Harjojudanto own 10 percent each.
Hasan named tobacco tycoon Putera Sampoerna and timber magnate Prajogo Pangestu as two of the large shareholders Nusamba would hold talks with.

Neither was available for comment but PT Hanjaya Mandala Sampoerna, a cigarette company headed by Putera Sampoerna, said on Saturday that it had cancelled a shareholders meeting scheduled for November 2 because it would "not pursue a course of action which would necessitate the convening of this meeting".

Sampoerna effectively controls the single largest stake in Astra. He announced last month that he had bought a 9.81 percent stake on his own account while PT Sampoerna said a wholly-owned subsidiary had bought an additional 2.85 percent.
Sources in PT Sampoerna said the meeting was to have discussed transactions related to Astra which would have required minority shareholder approval, and that it was no longer considered necessary.
Asked if this meant that Putera Sampoerna would join the syndicate proposed by Hasan, the sources said they were in no position to comment.
Brokers had said last month that PT Sampoerna had concluded arrangements for a new $400 million loan which could be used for further investment into Astra.
Pangestu is the next-largest shareholder in Astra, with his Delta Mustika company controlling a 10.68 percent stake.

A syndicate comprising Hasan, Sampoerna and Pangestu, among Indonesia's wealthiest men, would command at least over 32 percent of Astra, which brokers have said would be more than enough for effective control.
Astra's shareholdings are widely held, with Toyota Motor Co holding 8.26 percent. Astra shares closed on Friday at 4,000 rupiah ($1.74), down 50.
